quick-start.title: Quick start
quick-start.summary: Get an account, see how CoGA is organised, review a first case, and keep the five rules for safe use in mind.
paragraphs: Choose Sign in with Microsoft and use the Microsoft account of your hospital or university. Your first sign-in creates your CoGA account, with the role viewer: you read and change nothing. You see a project's data once an administrator gives you access to it, and you analyse once they give you a higher role.

Where the sign-in page offers Sign in with your organisation's account instead, your first sign-in also creates the account, and an administrator approves it. Where CoGA runs without either, choose Sign up on the sign-in page and fill in Create account. You can sign in once an administrator has activated the account and given you access to your projects.

Logout signs you out of CoGA, on every computer and in every browser where you are signed in: each of them asks you to sign in again. On a shared computer, then also choose Sign out of Microsoft (or of your organisation) on the sign-in page.

The arrow at the right of the top bar opens the main menu: Projects, Variant explorer, Gene explorer, CNV explorer, Panels, Report codes, User guide and, for superusers and administrators, Admin. Settings in the same bar holds your display preferences.
CoGA keeps the pedigree, the assay data and your interpretation together, so you review a case as a whole:
To set up a new case, see Case setup and data import.
blocks: Your role decides what you may do, lowest first: a viewer reads; an analyst also analyses (reviews, tags, classifications, HPO terms, the case's workflow); a supervisor also signs an analysis out; a superuser also has every project and the configuration the analyses read (gene panels, tags, preset filters, QC thresholds) and package import; an admin has the whole administration.

A project decides who sees the data and which reference assembly applies. You see only the projects you belong to; superusers and administrators see everything, and administrators create the projects. In each of your projects you are an analyst, who reads and changes its records as far as your role allows, or a reader, who only reads them. A family page says Read-only access where you only read: your role is viewer, or you are a reader there.
A family is the case: related samples with their pedigree, roles and affected status.
A sample carries the assay data: variants, coverage, segments, repeats and more.
Reference data (genes, cytobands, ClinVar, gnomAD, clinical CNVs and more) belongs to an assembly and is shared by all projects on it.
Review state — classifications, tags and notes — is your interpretation, kept per family.

Use CoGA safely. Decision support only. Review every suggestion, ranking and call; CoGA makes no diagnosis. Screening needs confirmation. Confirm an at-risk NIPT or carrier-screening finding with a diagnostic test. Validated scope only. A family marked Not validated for clinical use is outside the validated assembly (GRCh38) and cannot be signed out. Check Sample QC before sign-out: it confirms that the samples are who the pedigree says. Sign-out closes the analysis. It is the analytical sign-off, not the medical one: the clinical report is drafted and medically signed in the EPD and refers to the signed version. Only a supervisor of the family's project, a superuser or an administrator signs out; the laboratory decides who gets the supervisor role.
Decision support only. Review every suggestion, ranking and call; CoGA makes no diagnosis.
Screening needs confirmation. Confirm an at-risk NIPT or carrier-screening finding with a diagnostic test.
Validated scope only. A family marked Not validated for clinical use is outside the validated assembly (GRCh38) and cannot be signed out.
Check Sample QC before sign-out: it confirms that the samples are who the pedigree says.

Sign-out closes the analysis. It is the analytical sign-off, not the medical one: the clinical report is drafted and medically signed in the EPD and refers to the signed version. Only a supervisor of the family's project, a superuser or an administrator signs out; the laboratory decides who gets the supervisor role.
On the dashboard, search for a project, family or sample, and open the family.
On the family page, pick the analysis that fits the question. A button appears only when the family has that kind of data.
Check Sample QC before you interpret.
Build a shortlist in the variant list before you open the viewers.
Record your interpretation as you go: classification, tags and notes.
Tag the variants to report with Report, check the drafted report, and have a supervisor sign out the analysis. The clinical report follows in the EPD.

Not finding a variant you expect? The Small variants page opens with a default filter: the Phenotype priority preset on the Mendeliome panel (rare, HIGH or MODERATE impact, carried by the affected members). Press Clear all filters before you conclude that a variant is missing. The Variant explorer leaves out imputed calls unless you tick Include imputed variants.

case-setup.title: Case setup and data import
case-setup.summary: Create a family, import a data package, and know what each kind of data unlocks.
paragraphs: Choose the way in that matches how your data arrives.

The Package import page lists under Deliveries the family folders the pipelines delivered, each with its package file (coga-package.json), checked by CoGA. Nothing is imported until you approve it. A folder is listed once its check is done: CoGA reads the package's files whole, which takes up to an hour for a genome, and checks the smaller packages first.

CoGA keeps watching the folder after the import. A folder that changes, or is gone, is listed as Changed after import (on one row, the folder's new delivery's once there is one), and every page of the family warns of it (Package folder changed after import or Package folder gone); signing out meanwhile asks for a reason. See Family report and sign-out for what ends the warning. A file put into the folder later that the import reads, such as a CRAM, is listed by CoGA in the new delivery's package itself, with a warning: check it before you approve.
blocks: Build a new family by hand: add samples, set sex and roles, link parents and couples, and set affected and carrier status. Open to the analysts of a project whose role is analyst or higher, who add families to it, and to superusers and administrators; uploading a PED file here is for administrators.
A superuser or an administrator checks, corrects and approves the family folder a pipeline delivers to the CoGA server, or adds a folder by hand, and imports the family with all its data in one job.

Package import is for superusers and administrators. The rest of loading data is for administrators: single uploads on the Upload family and sample data page, and replacing an existing family, by a package import with Overwrite too. So is editing an existing family's members or structure. HPO terms are added, changed and removed by the analysts of the family's project (role analyst or higher), by superusers and by administrators.

For a monogenic NIPT case, tick Monogenic NIPT (cfDNA from maternal plasma) in the family builder and give the Pregnancy ID: see Monogenic NIPT. A family may hold several pregnancies of one woman, each pregnancy's NIPT an analysis of its own.

Each kind of data switches on part of CoGA: small variants: the small-variant page and Sample QC; structural variants: the SV page; TRGT calls: the repeat page; Paraphase: the paralogue page; mitochondrial calls: the mtDNA analysis; coverage, segments, APCAD and haplotypes: the viewer tracks. Any variant data also switches on the variant summary.
small variants: the small-variant page and Sample QC;
coverage, segments, APCAD and haplotypes: the viewer tracks.
Any variant data also switches on the variant summary.

Reference data first. Genes, cytobands, ClinVar and the other annotation layers are loaded per assembly. If a viewer cannot place coordinates or a gene search is empty, check that the reference data for the family's assembly is loaded.

Read the delivery's State (Ready, Needs attention, Still copying) and its warnings; a NIPT delivery names its pregnancy (· pregnancy ZW1). Add a folder by hand adds a folder no pipeline delivered (for a NIPT, give its Pregnancy ID); a folder that holds its own coga-package.json is not offered there, as it comes in under Deliveries.
Correct… completes or corrects what the package says (the project, the analysis, a NIPT's pregnancy, the members, the datasets), with a reason.

Dry run checks it as an import would, without writing anything. Approve… imports it, or tick several ready ones and press Approve selected. For a family that exists already, choose Update: add the missing datasets and members or, as an administrator, Overwrite: replace its datasets and pedigree. Refuse… sets a delivery aside, with a reason.

Follow the job under Recent family imports: the latest 10 jobs, up to 100 on Show all. A delivery whose import failed is offered again: checked again, it waits among the deliveries, naming the failed job; once the cause is fixed, approve it again (with Update when the failed import kept the family).

Overwrite: replace its datasets and pedigree

phenotype-matching.title: Phenotypes, panels and phenotype matching
phenotype-matching.summary: Record HPO terms, focus a search with a gene panel, and match the phenotype to genes and diseases with Monarch.
paragraphs: The patient's phenotype drives the ranking. Record it as HPO terms, and use gene panels to focus a search.
HPO terms are kept per person. An analyst of the family's project (role analyst or higher), a superuser or an administrator adds them:

Only present terms are used for matching. Each term added, changed or removed is an entry on the family's Clinical audit trail. A package import can bring terms in too: what it adds or changes is one entry per person, naming who ran the import and the package. A viewer or a reader sees the terms but cannot change them.

The Panel catalog holds reusable gene lists. Superusers and administrators create them or import them from PanelApp. To limit a search to a panel's genes, choose the panel in the Locations filter of the small-variant or structural-variant page.

The Mendeliome is the default scope of both pages: every gene that Monarch says causes a disease or is associated with one. A gene that Monarch links to a disease only as contributing to it or raising its likelihood is not in it.
On the small-variant and structural-variant pages and in the variant explorer, a panel of any size keeps:
So the Mendeliome, too, keeps a variant inside one of its genes whose annotation names another gene.

A panel names each gene by its HGNC symbol or by its Ensembl gene ID (ENSG and eleven digits), the gene's stable name. A gene name that no loaded assembly knows, such as a typo or an old symbol, gets no position. The panel's page lists it as not imported: a filter on the panel finds no variant in it. Use the current symbol or the Ensembl gene ID instead.

Superusers and administrators change a local panel's genes on its page, in three ways that can be combined: the bin on a gene's row, Add to changes for new names, and Edit the whole list. Each change is listed under Changes for version N, where a name no assembly knows is flagged. Nothing is saved until you press Confirm and save version N; the earlier version stays in the version history. If someone saved another version in the meantime, CoGA refuses the save, reloads the panel and keeps your changes listed, to confirm again.
CoGA uses the Monarch Initiative knowledge graph, which links genes, diseases and HPO phenotypes.
An administrator loads the Monarch data about monthly (Admin → Monarch data). Until it is loaded, the gene profile shows no associations and the ranking has no phenotype signal.
blocks: Click the person's sample name on the family page.
Under HPO phenotypes, search a term and choose present, absent or unknown.
Press Add phenotype. Edit changes a term's status or note: choose the new ones and press Save change. Remove takes a term off; to use another term, remove it and add that one.
the variants annotated with one of its genes;
the variants inside one of its regions: PanelApp's regions for the assembly, and each gene's position in the gene reference. A structural variant counts when it overlaps one.

On the gene profile (gene explorer), Monarch gene–disease associations lists each linked disease with its relationship, source and number of expected phenotypes. Opened from a family, it also says how many the family shows ("3 observed in family").

On the family page, the Phenotype match (Monarch) panel ranks candidate genes when you press Find candidate genes. It sends the HPO terms of every family member, not only the affected ones. Re-run match runs it again on the phenotypes recorded now, for example after you add one.
In the variant list, the Phenotype priority preset ranks variants partly by how well their gene matches the affected members' phenotypes (see Small-variant prioritisation).

Record specific phenotypes. A broad term such as Intellectual disability is linked to over a thousand genes and gives a weak ranking by design. Add the patient's distinctive features — a particular seizure type, a dysmorphic feature, a metabolic finding — and the ranking sharpens.

family-workspace.title: The family page
family-workspace.summary: The case hub: status and assignment, one button per analysis and viewer, the region of interest, and the family members.
paragraphs: Every case starts on its family page.

The family page, every analysis page (small and structural variants, repeat expansions, Paraphase, mtDNA, monogenic NIPT, the variant summary), the Sample QC and the report share one header. From any of them you can work on the case and move between analyses.

A row of links at the foot of the header leads to the family's analyses: Small variants, Structural variants, Repeat expansions, Paraphase, mtDNA analysis, Monogenic NIPT and, last, Variant summary (of all the family's variant data). At the far right of the same row, under the pedigree, are the family-level functions: Sample QC (when the family has small variants) and Report (when it has any variant data: small or structural variants, repeat expansions, Paraphase results or mtDNA data). A link appears only when the family has that kind of data. The page you are on is marked.

The ROI is the gene or locus the case is about; PGT uses it for the embryo calls. An administrator sets it (Save, Clear). Anyone can click it to open the chromosome view with 1 Mb on each side. In a PGT family, Review ROI markers → opens the marker review.

One row per sample: role, parents, partner, Related to, status, HPO terms and a Seq. QC chip, and Same individual when the family links two samples of one person (below). The chip shows the sequencing QC verdict and mean depth; hover or focus it for the metrics.

In a PGT family each embryo also shows its derived call (see Haplotype segregation). In a NIPT family the pregnancy's fetus has the role fetus and no data of its own; the pedigree draws a P in its symbol.

Related to names the member through whom a person is related by an unknown degree: for example a PGT index known to be on the mother's side, or both parents. The pedigree draws the link as a dotted arc with a ?. The haplotype track colours such a person:

Same individual names another sample of the same person: for example the plasma of a conventional NIPT under another sample ID than the monogenic NIPT's plasma of the same pregnancy, or the plasmas of two pregnancies of one woman. The pedigree draws the person as one symbol labelled with all its IDs (PLASMA1 / PLASMA2), with the sex, status and parents either sample records, and Sample QC expects the samples' genotypes identical, except a maternal plasma's, which it never compares. Two plasmas of one woman are one person, never one pregnancy: each pregnancy's results stay its own. The table keeps a row per sample. The samples of one person must agree on sex, affected and carrier status and parents, and are never also each other's relatives: a link, an edit or a package import that makes them differ is refused, and so is a father or mother role that the sex recorded on another of the person's samples contradicts.
Only an administrator edits the members, here and in Admin → Family & sample data, which shows this same table:

A changed row is marked changed, a new one new. Remove marks a member removed on save; Restore keeps it. When you save, CoGA shows what the removal affects (linked data, analyses that become stale) and asks you to confirm. A father is never a member recorded as female, nor a mother one recorded as male, so the lists do not offer them.

Affected status and carrier status are separate: an unaffected person can be a carrier. An analyst of the family's project (role analyst or higher) or a superuser adds, changes and removes HPO terms in the dialog; each term is saved on its own. The other fields are greyed out for them.
Further down are the Phenotype match (Monarch) panel and, closed by default, the Analysis pipeline settings recorded at import.
blocks: The trail above it (Dashboard / Families / project / family) names the family's project: click it to open the dashboard with that project's families shown.
One line gives the members, the assembly and the projects, then the page's own figures.

Status, Assigned to and Reviewed by track the case's workflow. An analyst of the family's project (role analyst or higher), a superuser or an administrator can change them; a viewer and a reader only see them.

Assigned to and Reviewed by offer the active analysts of the family's projects whose role is not viewer, the superusers and the administrators; never a reader or a viewer. Someone chosen before they became a reader or a viewer (or left the family's projects) stays shown, marked (not eligible), until you change it.
The one you choose under Assigned to gets an e-mail naming the family, with a link to it, when a mail server is set; not when you assign the family to yourself.
Read-only access in the header means you only read this family: your role is viewer, or you are a reader in its project.
A Not validated for clinical use banner shows when the family is outside the validated scope.

In a family of several analyses (short-read and then long-read WGS, or the NIPTs of several pregnancies of one woman), a page that reads one analysis at a time offers a list of the analyses beside the family name, with the analysis imported last shown first.

Curation gives one line each for the small variants, the structural variants, the repeat loci and the Paraphase regions: how many are reviewed, how many carry notes, and the count per review tag. For the repeat loci and the Paraphase regions it also counts how many carry your classification.
Visualization — Genome view, Chromosome view, Circos plot and IGV viewer.
A passing chip shows the number alone. Any other state is a word on the chip.
Warning or Fail: a metric crossed its limit, which the tooltip names.
Not run: the sample's QC was not assessed (no limit set for any of its metrics, or no verdict returned). This is never a pass.
An embryo whose QC holds only the PGT pipeline's embryo metrics has no depth to show. Its chip gives the value of the metric that decided the verdict (Fail ADO 14.2%), or Not run alone.
A sample sequenced in more than one analysis (short-read and then long-read WGS) has a chip of each, named by its analysis (Short-read WGS: Pass 35.0x). Each opens that analysis's QC report.
along the genome, when they turn out to be that member's own parent or child (they share one of the member's haplotypes along nearly every chromosome);
around the ROI only, when they are a more distant relative: there the markers on both sides show the haplotype they share. Elsewhere such a relative stays grey.

Press Edit members. Each row turns into its fields: role, sex, father, mother, partner, Related to, Same individual, affected status, carrier status and, for a carrier, its type. A last row adds a member. Same individual offers the members of the same sex or of unknown sex (in the last row, of the sex chosen for the new member); a choice replaces the member's link, so link a person with three samples one pair at a time.
Or click a sample name to open Family member details: the same fields, the sample ID and the HPO terms. A change there shows in the table at once.
Press Save changes. Everything goes in one change of the family's structure, with one entry on its clinical audit trail. Discard drops the changes.

sample-qc.title: Sample-integrity QC
sample-qc.summary: Check, before you interpret, that the samples are who the pedigree says: swaps, wrong relationships, wrong sex and consanguinity.
paragraphs: Open a family and press Sample QC to check that the samples are who the pedigree says. A swapped tube, a wrong parent, a mislabelled sex or unexpected relatedness quietly invalidates everything downstream, so run it before you interpret.

It does not measure contamination. Some results can be a sign of it, among other causes: a high Mendelian-error rate, or heterozygous calls on a man's X that leave his genetic sex indeterminate or female. A pass does not rule contamination out.
The page first works out what kind of case it is and runs only the checks that fit:

Two samples linked as the same individual count as one person here: one person sampled twice is a single sample, a couple with a partner sampled twice a carrier couple. The two samples of one person are compared in every kind of case, a single sample's included (see Relatedness vs pedigree).
The checks read the family's genotypes (Read from in the header names the call set and the number of sites). A genotype with a quality (GQ) below 20 counts as a no-call.
blocks: Family with parents — sex, relatedness against the pedigree, Mendelian errors.
Shallow-WGS PGT — embryo sex and parentage (each embryo a child of both parents), Mendelian errors.
Monogenic NIPT — paternity, fetal sex, parent sex and a check of the cfDNA categories, one pregnancy at a time: in a family of several, choose it in the analysis list beside the family name.
Conventional NIPT — no check: ccnv's output holds no genotypes, and the fetal sex is known only from the analysis, as an embryo's is in PGT.
Carrier couple — sex per partner, and that the two are unrelated.
The verdict at the top — the worst of the checks. A check that could not run counts as a warning, never as a pass. A note names each sample whose sex could not be checked.

Pedigree & sample integrity — each person's symbol carries a ring and a badge: green ✓ pass, amber ! warning, red ✕ fail. A check that could not run counts as a warning here too. A person drawn with several samples (linked as the same individual) carries the worst of its samples. Hover a symbol for the reason.

Family members & per-sample checks — recorded sex against genetic sex, and the Mendelian-error rate. The genetic sex carries green ✓ when it matches the record, red ✗ when it does not, amber ! when it could not be confirmed and grey ? when it was not checked. Hover a cell for the reason. A sample without X genotypes (for example in a PGT family) is sexed from its reads by the pipeline's ngs-bits; the reason says so. An embryo has sex 0 (unknown) in the family's PED: its genetic sex shows the sex its data indicate, with ✓ (Embryo's sex not recorded), and amber ! only when the data tell no sex.

Relatedness vs pedigree (Parentage (embryos ↔ parents) in a PGT family) — each pair's inferred relationship, kinship and IBS0. A pair that contradicts the pedigree, including parents who look related, is outlined: red for a fail, amber for a warning. A first-degree pair reads as parent–child when its IBS0 is below an eighth of the IBS0 of the family's unrelated parents, or below a fixed 0.8% without them; otherwise as siblings. The pair's message gives the cut. Two samples recorded as the same individual pass when their genotypes look a duplicate (Duplicate / same individual / MZ twin in the legend), and fail otherwise: a possible sample swap. Too few shared sites to compare them is a warning that stops sign-out until someone records a reason. A maternal plasma is never compared: it is a mixture of the mother's DNA and a fetus's, so two plasmas of one woman are one person but are never expected identical. What the pedigree records of a person (its parents, children, siblings, co-parent) is expected of each of its samples, with each sample of the other person.
Paternity, Fetal sex and cfDNA category QC — for a cfDNA family.

Sequencing & embryo QC — under its own heading in the per-sample table: each sample's sequencing QC as its pipeline reported it, one column per measure. These are mean depth and alignment and, for a PGT embryo, its allele drop-out (ADO) and drop-in (ADI) and its Mendelian concordance with its parents before and after imputation: the numbers of the pipeline's dashboard. A value outside the lab's cut-off shows its verdict; a value without a cut-off is shown, not judged. Seq. QC is the sample's worst. A sample sequenced in more than one analysis (short-read and then long-read WGS) shows each analysis's value, named, each judged against that analysis's cut-offs. These values do not change the sample's status or the overall verdict, and do not stop sign-out. The signed report records every value.

What to do with a warning or a fail. A fail points to a real problem: re-check the sample sheet, the pedigree and the genotypes before you interpret. A warning usually means too little data to decide (few informative sites, a low fetal fraction, a check that could not run); it weakens the analysis but does not invalidate it. A fail, or a check of the pedigree or of a sample's identity that could not run (a NIPT parent's sex, for example), also stops sign-out until someone records a reason.
inline: What to do with a warning or a fail.

small-variant-filtering.title: Small-variant prioritisation
small-variant-filtering.summary: The small-variant page: the default view, the filters and presets, the phenotype-driven ranking, and genes also hit by a structural variant.
paragraphs: Most candidates are found on the Small variants page. The filters take a genome down to a short list; the Phenotype priority preset puts it in order.
The page opens with the Phenotype priority (Exomiser-style) preset on the Mendeliome panel:

A family can hold several analyses, on the same DNA or on different samples of one person: short-read and then long-read WGS, for instance. Each stays apart. When two or more of them have small variants of their own, the page reads one analysis at a time: pick it in the list beside the family's name (the analysis imported last is shown first). The list, its counts, the filters, the ranking and the CSV export are that analysis's alone (a callset filter reads only the analysis's own callsets), and a review you save is that analysis's review: a variant both callsets hold has a review in each analysis, and each sign-out freezes its own. An inheritance filter reads the members the analysis's package lists. The Variant summary offers the same list for its small-variant counts, and on the workspace each curation line names the analysis whose reviews it counts. The Structural variants page reads one at a time the analyses with structural variants of their own (the conventional NIPT of each pregnancy), from a list of its own. The links between the family's pages keep the analysis you read, and the genome view reads the analysis the page you came from named.

A member the analysis's package lists can still have no calls in it: long-read WGS of the proband alone whose package lists the parents. A note above the results names such members. An inheritance filter reads a call it does not find as reference, so while one is applied the note warns, for instance: The parents (MOTHER and FATHER1) have no calls in the long-read WGS analysis: the inheritance filter reads their missing calls as reference, so it cannot leave out variants inherited from them. An affected member without calls leaves the filter no variant at all. The Inheritance row says the same, and the CSV export names those members in its last column, Members without calls.

The filters sit under Advanced filters, closed when the page opens, one category to a row across the page: Phenotype, Structural second hit, Inheritance, Pathogenicity, Annotations, In silico, Frequency, Call quality, Locations, Exclude and Review and curation. Closed, Advanced filters says how many categories have a filter set. A row's bar says how many filters its category holds and carries its quick choice at the right; click the bar for the category's fields. A category with a filter set is marked red at the left of its bar. Expand all and Collapse all open or close every row.

For de novo and dominant, a male's call on chrX or chrY outside the pseudo-autosomal regions (1 or 1/1) counts as one copy. A location entry that cannot be read (for example an end before its start) is named under its field, and nothing is searched until you fix it. A per-sample minimum (GQ, DP, AF or AD alt) that is not a number fails the search, and the message names it.

The annotation filters must all hold on one transcript of the variant: impact and consequence, the transcript, HGVS, Canonical only, MANE only and LoF only, the ClinVar status, the in-silico scores and the frequencies. So with MANE only and HIGH impact, a variant whose HIGH-impact transcript is not its MANE transcript is left out.

A card, a table row and a CSV row describe one transcript of the variant: MANE Select, else the canonical one, else the most severe. The filters may have held on another. For example, deleterious keeps a variant whose MANE transcript SIFT calls tolerated when a second transcript is deleterious; HIGH or MODERATE impact keeps one that is synonymous on its MANE transcript and missense on another. In that case:

Filters met on names a transcript whose own impact, consequence and scores meet the filters: a variant that only the ClinVar override keeps names none. The ranking and ACMG classify read the transcript the row describes.

The built-in presets are Phenotype priority, Dominant strict, Dominant relaxed, Expanded carrier screening, Compound het, Recessive hom, Recessive broad, Any affected and ClinVar review. A preset saves the recipe, not the result; save your own to standardise a search. Compound-heterozygous candidates, also under All, compound het grouped, and the findings of Expanded carrier screening are listed by gene. Up to 100 results show as cards, more as a table; Table and Cards above the list switch between the two. A gene counts as one result.

At the top of the page, Showing counts the results, and Variants and Genes count what the filters keep: the variants, and the genes they are in. Each variant counts toward the gene its card names; a variant without a gene counts toward none. A count with a + is a lower bound. Above the list, Results gives the number of results, or, when the variants outnumber the results, the number of genes and of variants (for example 9 genes · 30 variants).

A gene is a frame headed by the gene, as a single card is, with its diseases and inheritance once, and holds each of its variants as the list of single variants shows it: as its full card, headed by its place (Variant 1 of 3) and its change, or as a row of the table. Fold the frame to its heading and the changes of its variants, or fold one card inside it.

A compound-het gene holds every variant of its pairs once. Its lines say which parent each variant came from (Paternal, Maternal; Parent not traced where the parents' genotypes cannot tell), and each card carries the same label. Then each pair that can be the recessive cause has a line of its own: its phase, as the reads or the parents place it, and the pair review it holds, with the phase recorded there. Two variants from the father and three from the mother are one gene with five variants and six pairs: each paternal variant with each maternal one. Two variants from one parent are in cis and form no pair.

A card takes its colour from ClinVar, here and on the monogenic NIPT page: light red when ClinVar calls the variant pathogenic or likely pathogenic, light green when it calls it benign or likely benign. Classifications that disagree, such as uncertain significance & likely pathogenic, are a conflict: light orange when one of them is pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Any other conflicting, uncertain or other ClinVar status, or none, leaves the card white. In the table a row is tinted the same way, more faintly, and the ClinVar chip takes the same colour.

Beside the ClinVar of the variant's annotation, a card shows CoGA's own ClinVar release, the one CoGA loads from NCBI's weekly file. Each value is named by its release: ClinVar (annotation, 2026-05-01), the ClinVar file the pipeline annotated, and ClinVar (CoGA, 2026-11-22). CoGA's is matched on the exact allele, never on the rsID or the position. It links to its ClinVar record, gives the review status and the conditions on hover, and is marked changed when its classification or stars differ from the annotation's. Without a value it says why: not in this release, no release loaded, or not available for this assembly; a variant ClinVar classifies only as part of a combination says so. More annotations & detail lists CoGA's review status and conditions. In the table and the Variant Explorer a ≠ beside the variant marks one whose two classifications differ, CoGA's on hover. Every page shows one CoGA release: the one current when the page was asked for.

Under its heading, a card names up to three diseases its gene is linked to: Monarch's causal links, those more sources back first; else the gene's OMIM diseases; else Monarch's associations, marked not causal. Each name opens the disease in Monarch, or in OMIM for an OMIM disease. +N more opens More annotations & detail, which lists every Monarch and OMIM link. No gene–disease link cached means CoGA's copy of Monarch and OMIM holds none for the gene.

The line below names the gene's Inheritance: each mode a GenCC or ClinGen curation classified Definitive, Strong, Moderate or Supportive gives it, dominant and recessive each in a colour of its own. Hover a mode for the curations behind it. None curated in GenCC or ClinGen means the gene has a disease but no such curation. Where ClinGen has curated the gene's dosage, ClinGen dosage shows its haploinsufficiency (HI) and triplosensitivity (TS) scores and opens the curation. A gene on the ACMG secondary-findings list has a chip such as ACMG SF v3.3; hover it for the list's phenotype, category, inheritance and variants to report. The ACMG SF list could not be read means no chip does not tell you the gene is off the list; the gene page says which.
The card's columns:

Expanded carrier screening is for couples only. The couple is the two partners the family links as a couple, else its mother and father, else its two people. Two samples linked as the same individual are one person, never a couple: a family of one person sampled twice has no couple. A partner sampled twice carries what either of their samples in the analysis you read carries. It keeps:

Each gene is one result, with every variant either partner carries there: two, three or more. Its frame says why the gene is a finding (Both partners, X-linked) and which variants each partner carries; each variant's card names the partner who carries it, in that partner's colour.

A ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic call overrides the frequency and impact cut-offs, so a common founder variant and a pathogenic synonymous or splice-region variant stay in. A ClinVar benign or likely benign variant is left out, so it never makes a gene one both partners carry a variant in. The X-linked rule does not read the partners' recorded sex. Mitochondrial variants are not part of it, as mtDNA passes from the mother alone.

Your saved searches are shared with the monogenic NIPT page. A search saved there can carry filters that only the NIPT list applies: an inheritance view such as De novo in the fetus, the maternal/fetal categories, the minimum confidence. This page does not send them and shows no chip for them; it names them once under the active filters. De novo in the fetus is not De novo / dominant, which reads the family members' own genotypes.

With Phenotype priority on, a Score column appears and the rows are ranked, best first. The score combines the variant's own evidence (impact and predictors, ClinVar, rarity, fit with the pedigree) with how well its gene matches the affected members' HPO terms. A ✦ marks a gene that matches. Hover the score, or read the card, for the breakdown: Variant, Pathogenicity, Rarity and Phenotype, the compatible inheritance modes and the matched phenotypes.

Why the ranking can be instant. CoGA stores a ranking once computed; a later open shows ⚡ Prioritised ranking served from cache and when it was computed. It is recomputed automatically when anything it depends on changes: the phenotypes, the pedigree, the panel's genes and regions, the filters (including review-tag filters), the family's variant data, or the reference data (the Monarch release, each import of the HPO ontology, gene constraint, and the gene positions a panel or an excluded gene uses).

Narrowing from the Mendeliome to a smaller panel reuses the broader ranking, ranked from 1 within the smaller panel, as long as the Mendeliome's genes and regions have not changed since that ranking was computed. The smaller panel gets its own ranking instead when it reaches a variant the broader ranking lacks (through a region of its own, such as the position PanelApp gives for a gene), or keeps one variant of a compound-het pair without the other.

Download CSV exports the list, with Priority, Variant score and Rank columns when the ranking is on, in the order it was ranked by. Its Classification column holds the class each review shows on the page, Classification text the classification as typed, and Tags the review's tags. HGVSg is VEP's HGVS.g; it is empty where the annotation has none, since the CSV gives the position and alleles in their own columns.

A small variant whose gene is also hit by an SV carries an SV badge (for example SV: DEL), with a trans or cis chip when a phase was decided. Also hit by an SV, under Structural second hit, keeps only these genes. The phase comes from read phasing or from the parents' genotypes, by the same rule as for compound-het pairs; the reference gives the rule. Each SV of the gene gets its own phase, listed in the badge's explanation. A deletion in trans with the SNV marks the gene effectively biallelic, whatever the other SVs are.
blocks: gnomAD exome, genome and popmax frequency 1% or below, and at most 10 homozygotes and 10 hemizygotes;
a ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic record overrides the impact and frequency cut-offs, so a pathogenic synonymous or splice-region variant and a common founder variant stay in;
ClinVar benign and likely benign left out;
carried (het or hom) by each affected member, with genotype quality (GQ) 20, depth 10, allele balance 0.2 and 4 alt reads or more;
inheritance All, compound het grouped: the compound-het pairs among the results are listed by gene, each gene where its best-ranked variant ranks, and every other variant on its own.

The default view hides variants. A variant outside the Mendeliome, a common variant, a low-quality call, or a variant an affected member does not carry is not shown. Press Clear all filters before you conclude that a variant is not in the data.

Inheritance has the inheritance model as its quick choice. All, compound het grouped keeps every variant the other filters keep, as All does, and lists the compound-het pairs among them by gene, as Compound heterozygous does. Every other variant stays a single result. The Phenotype priority and Any affected presets set it.

Annotations groups the VEP consequences as seqr does: nonsense, essential splice site, frameshift, missense, in frame, synonymous, extended splice site, other, motif feature and regulatory feature. A group's own box ticks or clears all its terms. Beside them are the VEP impacts (HIGH, MODERATE, LOW, MODIFIER), the SpliceAI minimum, and Canonical only, MANE only and LoF only. A saved search's term that no box offers is listed under Other selected terms, ticked. Its Quick choice sets the consequences and the impacts together, and leaves the SpliceAI minimum and the three switches as they are. All clears both. High impact ticks HIGH, and Moderate to high impact HIGH and MODERATE, with no consequence. All coding ticks the coding consequences (missense, frameshift, stop gained, stop lost, start lost, splice acceptor, donor and region, in-frame insertion and deletion, protein altering, synonymous and coding sequence variant), with no impact. Any other selection shows as Custom.

Its Quick choice sets the consequences and the impacts together, and leaves the SpliceAI minimum and the three switches as they are. All clears both. High impact ticks HIGH, and Moderate to high impact HIGH and MODERATE, with no consequence. All coding ticks the coding consequences (missense, frameshift, stop gained, stop lost, start lost, splice acceptor, donor and region, in-frame insertion and deletion, protein altering, synonymous and coding sequence variant), with no impact. Any other selection shows as Custom.

Frequency has a slider per population. In its header, AF sets every population at once; AC and H/H set gnomAD's allele count and its homozygote and hemizygote counts. AF shows the maximum shared by the populations that have one, or mixed when they differ. A maximum count keeps a variant without that count, as absent from gnomAD. When such a variant may be in gnomAD after all, a note above the list says how many passed unchecked (Passed the gnomAD count filter unchecked); hover it for what it counts.

A maximum count keeps a variant without that count, as absent from gnomAD. When such a variant may be in gnomAD after all, a note above the list says how many passed unchecked (Passed the gnomAD count filter unchecked); hover it for what it counts.

Call quality sets the minimum genotype quality, allele balance, depth and alt reads of the members' calls, for all members at once or per member. With Affected only on, only the affected members' calls are held to them, so a parent's reference call is not held to an allele balance it cannot have. Switched off, every member gets the minimums the affected members share. Pass variants only, under Filter value, keeps a variant when every member's call that carries it passed its caller's FILTER (PASS, or no filter set), whatever Affected only says. Only the family's members count: a sample taken out of the family, or not yet added, holds nothing back. A callset of one file per sample gives each call its own FILTER, so a parent's reference call (DeepVariant's RefCall) holds nothing back. A multi-sample VCF gives the FILTER of the site. The quick choices High quality and Passing turn it on, as in seqr; All variants turns it off.

With Affected only on, only the affected members' calls are held to them, so a parent's reference call is not held to an allele balance it cannot have. Switched off, every member gets the minimums the affected members share.

Pass variants only, under Filter value, keeps a variant when every member's call that carries it passed its caller's FILTER (PASS, or no filter set), whatever Affected only says. Only the family's members count: a sample taken out of the family, or not yet added, holds nothing back. A callset of one file per sample gives each call its own FILTER, so a parent's reference call (DeepVariant's RefCall) holds nothing back. A multi-sample VCF gives the FILTER of the site.
The quick choices High quality and Passing turn it on, as in seqr; All variants turns it off.

Review and curation keeps a variant by the class its review, or its compound-het pair's review, shows. A class word typed as the classification (VUS) gives its class; otherwise the review's class tag gives it, the most severe of two; otherwise the classification as typed. So Likely pathogenic - class 4 also finds a variant classified by its class tag alone, and not one classified as VUS - class 3 beside the Pathogenic - class 5 tag: that variant shows class 5. Capitals do not matter.

Under In silico, one of the predictors you set is enough. The SpliceAI minimum, set under Annotations, counts as one of them. A SpliceAI score at that minimum also passes the impact and consequence filter.

A SIFT or PolyPhen choice keeps a transcript whose prediction is exactly that one, whatever score VEP wrote after it. deleterious keeps deleterious(0.01) but not deleterious_low_confidence(0.03), which is a choice of its own; tolerated leaves out tolerated_low_confidence.

The gene, the rsID and the excluded ClinVar statuses apply to the variant as a whole. A gene keeps every variant annotated with it, including one VEP places just outside the gene (upstream or downstream), ranked or not.

ClinVar pathogenic / likely pathogenic overrules the frequency, consequence and in-silico filters, under Frequency and on by default: a transcript with a ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic record passes the impact, consequence and SpliceAI filter, the in-silico filter and every frequency and gnomAD count, whatever its values. The other filters still apply to it: the transcript, HGVS, Canonical only, MANE only, LoF only, the ClinVar status, the genotypes. A variant whose allele CoGA's own ClinVar release (ClinVar (CoGA), below) calls pathogenic or likely pathogenic passes the same filters on every one of its transcripts, so a variant ClinVar reclassified after the pipeline annotated it is not left out.

Pathogenicity also offers ClinVar (CoGA) status: the classifications of CoGA's own ClinVar release, with the same choices. It keeps a variant one of whose alleles that release classifies so; without a loaded release it keeps none. The monogenic NIPT page does not offer it: NIPT reads the annotation's ClinVar.

the card (under its transcript) and the table row (under its effect) say Filters met on, with the transcript the filters held on and its consequence, LoF and in-silico predictions that differ from the row's. The row's own values stay as they are;
the card's transcript list marks that transcript Filters met;
the CSV gives it in its last columns, Filter-matched transcript to Filter-matched PolyPhen.
MANE only needs GRCh38. MANE only keeps a variant with a MANE Select or MANE Plus Clinical transcript. VEP sets these flags on GRCh38 only, so on a GRCh37 or T2T family MANE only keeps nothing.

Variant opens with the gene's ID and the transcript the card describes, then gives HGVS.g, HGVS.c and HGVS.p. HGVS.c and HGVS.p are on that transcript, without its accession. HGVS.g is VEP's (its HGVSg) where the annotation has it; otherwise it is written from the VCF record and is not HGVS-normalised. Hover the label to see which.
Frequencies: a filter row under a gnomAD frequency means the site fails gnomAD's own QC (AC0, RF …): gnomAD itself does not trust that frequency.

In silico: a dot before each prediction shows how it reads, in seqr's colours: green and olive benign, grey indeterminate, yellow, red and dark red pathogenic (supporting, moderate, strong). The thresholds are seqr's, from ClinGen's calibration of the predictors; SpliceAI uses the cut-offs of CoGA's ACMG evaluation. pLI and Missense Z describe the gene and have no dot.
the genes where both partners carry a rare (below 1%) high- or moderate-impact variant;

the variants either partner carries on chrX outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, each on its own: a woman's carrier status alone puts a son at risk of an X-linked condition, and a man passes his X to every daughter.

A search can stop part-way. Compound-het and recessive pairing, All, compound het grouped and Expanded carrier screening read at most 5,000 candidates before they filter, ranked or not. When a search reaches that limit, a warning above the results says "Results may be incomplete" and after how many candidates the search stopped. The count is then a lower bound (for example 12+), and a match beyond the limit is not shown. Narrow the filters with a region, a gene panel or a gene until the warning is gone.

A gene without Monarch data gets no phenotype credit and ranks lower; its Variant score is not affected. To find such novel-gene candidates, set Rank by in the Phenotype filters to Variant score: the whole ranking, not only the page shown, is then ordered by the variant score, the phenotype match left out of the order. The scores stay the same; the Score column and each card show the variant score and the rank in that order, and a note above the list says it is ranked so. The CSV export of a ranked list writes both scores and the rank.
Without HPO terms on the affected members, the ranking uses the variant evidence only.

The ranking changes the order of a search, not what it finds. With an inheritance mode or Expanded carrier screening it ranks the same variants and compound-het pairs the search finds without it. A gene is listed where its best-ranked variant ranks; each variant shows its own rank.
The score orders candidates within the family; it is not a probability of pathogenicity.

A warning that "Ranking may be incomplete" means more candidates matched than CoGA ranks at once (it says how many were ranked), so the best one may be missing. Narrow the filters: a region, a panel, a gene, or a tighter frequency or impact.
Also hit by a structural variant
inline: The parents (MOTHER and FATHER1) have no calls in the long-read WGS analysis: the inheritance filter reads their missing calls as reference, so it cannot leave out variants inherited from them.
Passed the gnomAD count filter unchecked
ClinVar pathogenic / likely pathogenic overrules the frequency, consequence and in-silico filters
None curated in GenCC or ClinGen
The ACMG SF list could not be read

interpretation-and-review.title: Interpretation and review
interpretation-and-review.summary: Tag, annotate and classify variants — with the semi-automatic ACMG classifier — and keep the review state per family.
paragraphs: Record your interpretation as you go. Review state is kept per family: the same variant in two families has two separate records. In a family of several analyses (short-read and then long-read WGS of the same DNA), it is kept per analysis too: a review belongs to the analysis you review the variant in, and is in that analysis's signed version only. A variant both analyses hold has a review in each you review it in, each with its own classification, tags and note. A review made before the family held an analysis counts in each analysis until you review the variant there.

Each row or card has Review, Exclude and Report (one-click tags), Tags & notes and ACMG classify. An excluded variant stays in the list. Its card folds to its heading and a bar marked Excluded, with who excluded it and on which day: Show card unfolds it, and Undo exclude takes the tag off again. In the table view its row is dimmed.

To go through the list one card at a time, fold each card when you are done with it: Collapse, at the foot of the card, folds it to its heading and the change (HGVS.c and HGVS.p), and the next card is the first open one. The caret before a card's heading folds and opens it too, an excluded card's included; a compound-het gene or a carrier screen's gene folds from its caret to its heading and the changes of its variants, and each card in it folds on its own. A fold changes no review and is saved nowhere: the cards you folded open again when you load the page anew. The small-variant and monogenic NIPT cards fold alike.
ACMG classify opens a dialog that pre-evaluates the ACMG/AMP criteria from the variant, the gene and the family genotypes, and scores them on the ClinGen points scale.
A variant opened from the mtDNA analysis page gets a mitochondrial rule set.

The structural-variant page works the same way: Review, Exclude, Report, tags and notes, and ACMG (CNV) for the ClinGen copy-number classifier. Saving a CNV classification also freezes its evidence, so the report can tell whether it changed. An event called by more than one caller is listed once per caller, with one shared review; the classification freezes the evidence of the row you opened it from. Small-variant and SV review are counted separately on the family page.
blocks: Tags. The built-in tags are Review, Send for validation, Validated, Validation did not confirm, Confident AR single hit, Excluded and Report, the ACMG class tags, the VUS tiers and Secondary finding. A superuser or an administrator can add custom tags for one project or for everyone. A renamed custom tag stays on every review that holds it. A deleted one stays too, marked (deleted): untick it to remove it from a review. It can no longer be added.

Class. A row or card shows the review's class once. A class word typed as the classification (VUS) gives its class; otherwise the review's class tag gives it, the most severe of two; otherwise the classification as typed. A class tag of another class is not shown beside it. The VUS tiers and Secondary finding are tags, never the class. The filters, the Variant Explorer and Download CSV read the class the same way; the CSV also gives the classification as typed, in Classification text.

Review, Exclude and Report change the tags only: the classification stays as stored. Tags & notes opens on the class shown. Choosing another class there, or none, replaces the classification and every class tag; left alone, the save keeps both as they are.
Notes keep your reasoning with the variant.

Who and when. A card shows its tags and note first, just under its heading, each with who added it and on which day; one analyst's tags of one day share one line. Review and Report show there too, beside their pressed buttons; who excluded a variant is on its Excluded bar. A note stays its writer's until someone changes it: adding a tag or a class does not make it theirs.
Report puts the variant in the family report.

Each criterion shows as checked (the data supports it), ● (consider), ✕ (the data argues against) or n/a (cannot apply). Hover it for the evidence; click to change it, and pick its strength. Only checked criteria count.

Some criteria are never applied together, such as PS2 and PM6, or PVS1 and PP3. Checking one unchecks the other, which then shows ⊘; hover it for the reason. PM1 and PP3 together count at most Strong: setting one lowers the other to fit.

A de novo variant is PS2 where the Sample QC confirms the proband's parents, and PM6 where it does not. Its strength follows ClinGen's de novo points: how specific the proband's phenotype is for the gene, from the gene–phenotype match score.

A variant without a gnomAD frequency is PM2 (absent from gnomAD) only on chromosomes 1–22, X and Y of a callset annotated with gnomAD's genomes or its joint set. Elsewhere PM2 is offered as ● (consider): check gnomAD before you apply it.
The bar at the top shows the points, the class and, for a VUS, the tier (hot, warm or cold).

Under it, the Evidence cards show the data the criteria are weighed on: the consequence and transcript, the population frequencies (gnomAD AF and FAF95, homozygotes, the in-house cohort), the in silico scores (REVEL, CADD, AlphaMissense, SpliceAI, with the variant card's coloured dots), the gene's inheritance and constraint, ClinVar, the proband's HPO terms and the gene–phenotype match, each member's genotype and what the Sample QC says of the proband's parents. Each card names the criteria it informs. A value the annotation does not hold shows as —. Fold the cards away to see only the criteria.

The header links to gnomAD, ClinVar, DECIPHER and a PubMed search on the gene and the patient's HPO terms. ClinVar, here and on the variant card, opens the record the annotation matched. Without one it searches ClinVar for the change on a RefSeq transcript (NM_…:c.…): the variant's own, or the one MANE pairs with its Ensembl transcript. Else it searches for the rsID, else for every record at the variant's position on GRCh38 or GRCh37. ClinVar knows no Ensembl transcript.

Save classification stores the class as the variant's classification and review tag, with every criterion and your note; the server recomputes the class. It also freezes the evidence the dialog read — the ClinVar significance, the consequence and LoF call, the population frequencies, the in-silico scores and, for a missense variant, the gene's missense Z — so the report can later tell whether it changed, and what.
Opening a classified variant again shows the criteria as you saved them.
Decision support, not an autoclassifier. The dialog pre-positions the criteria; you confirm them, adjust the strengths and add a note.

clinical-report.title: Family report and sign-out
clinical-report.summary: Draft the family report from the tagged variants, see what changed, and sign the analysis out into a version that can never change. The clinical report is signed in the EPD.
paragraphs: Tag a variant with Report to add it to the family report (the Report button on the family page). The live report drafts text per reported variant — description, ACMG reasoning, gene context and phenotype overlap — and is where you sign out the analysis. After sign-out, the Report button opens the signed version.

Sign-out closes the analysis; the medical sign-off is in the EPD. Sign out report is the analytical sign-off: it closes the analysis and freezes it into a signed version. The clinical report is drafted and medically signed in the hospital's electronic patient record (EPD), not in CoGA. It refers to exactly one signed version: the one it rests on.
Sign out report freezes the reported result into a numbered version with a unique fingerprint. The version also holds what the analysis looked at:
The EPD refers to the signed version by its report code (for example 7KQM2X-2-4PHT). Sign-out stops for seven things:

Your acknowledgement covers exactly what its dialog lists. If the concerns change before you click Sign out anyway, nothing is signed out: the dialog shows the current concerns, says they changed, and asks for your reason again.

A PGT embryo call whose phasing QC does not meet its thresholds (⚠ phasing QC on the family page) does not stop sign-out: the call stands, you decide on it, and the signed version records the warning.

Every reason you give is frozen into the signed version and written to the audit trail. Signing out again (Amend sign-out) creates a new version; earlier versions are never overwritten. A clinical report that rests on the amended analysis refers to the new version. After sign-out the page shows the signed version and its report code: quote that code in the EPD report. A mistyped code is refused as a typo, never taken for another record's. Report codes in the main menu finds the signed version a code names.

A family of several analyses. A family that holds more than one analysis (the monogenic and the conventional NIPT of each pregnancy of one woman, or short-read and then long-read WGS) signs each out on its own. Its signed version freezes that analysis's data only, and the checks read that analysis's data only. Data no analysis claims as its own, such as an upload, count for every analysis. Its reported variants are those its own reviews tag Report: a variant reported in one analysis is not in another's signed version unless you review it there too. Sign out a pregnancy's monogenic NIPT on its NIPT report and every other analysis here. When several remain, pick one under Analysis to sign out; the button names it (Sign out the conventional NIPT of pregnancy ZW1). Sign-out of each analysis lists each analysis with its latest signed version, report code, signer and date, and whether the family's data still match it.

Only the signed version is. A signed case opens on its latest signed version, drawn from the frozen record: Signed version N — signed out by … on …, with its report code and fingerprint. It shows what was signed:
It says what the record does not hold — the population frequencies and predictions, the gene and phenotype context, the audit trail — and never fills that in from current data.

Of a family of several analyses, the page opens on the latest signed version of the analyses it signs out. A signed version names its analysis (Clinical report — signed version 2 of the conventional NIPT of pregnancy ZW1), and its latest and its check are that analysis's, as are its annotation versions. Where the repeat expansions or Paraphase results are another analysis's, the section holds none and says so of its analysis (The short-read WGS had no repeat-expansion calls.): the other analysis's record freezes them. Print signed version N prints it; Download signed version N (JSON) returns the record itself. Signed versions lists the earlier ones.

Open the live report shows the current data. It says This is the live report, not signed version N, and whether it still matches: amber when something changed since (it names what), grey when the check could not be made (treat it as unsigned). Its printout starts with Not the signed report.
blocks: Every reported variant, small and structural. If a list cannot hold them all, an Incomplete warning says so, on screen and in print, so a printout cannot pass for the whole list.

Each variant's class as the family page shows it: a class word in the classification (VUS), else its class tag, else the text. When the ACMG classification, or a structural variant's CNV scoring, gives another class, that score stands beside it: VUS - class 3 (ACMG score: Likely pathogenic - class 4 · 8 pts). A structural variant whose review shows no class reads Not classified, even with a CNV score.

The repeat expansions and Paraphase findings marked Report: gene and disease, every member's call with CoGA's status, your classification and note, and the marks differs from CoGA's status and Changed since review where they apply. Without any, the section says so.

A provenance footer, printed with the report: the CoGA version that produced the page, the in-house IVD statement and the manufacturer, and the versions behind the data: the pipeline tools, the Reference assembly (the genome the pipeline aligned to, where it names one), the gene loci, the Monarch release and the HPO release.

An evidence-drift banner when a classification's evidence changed after it was made: for example a new ClinVar significance, REVEL score or gnomAD frequency (REVEL 0.412 → 0.951), consequence or LoF call (LoF LC → HC), missense Z for a missense variant's gene, or a structural variant that now overlaps other genes. Re-review those variants.

The Clinical audit trail: who classified, tagged or annotated what, who reviewed a compound-heterozygous pair, who changed the pedigree or the family's phenotypes, and when. Entries can never be changed or deleted. Only analysts, superusers and administrators see it; a viewer, or a reader of the family's project, sees on screen and in print that it is not shown. It opens on the 200 most recent entries; when there are more, it says how many it shows, and Show older events loads the next 200. A printout of only part of the trail says so.
The Analysis pipeline settings recorded at import.

An Import incomplete warning at the top when a data import left the family partly loaded or has not finished (still running, or stopped part-way, for example by a server restart). It names the import job and the datasets that failed or were not finished. It also names: a single upload that has not finished, or that failed and could not put back what it deleted, as a single-file upload; an unfinished deletion of the family's data, as a deletion of this family's data: an administrator's deletion of a sample or of the family, a PED upload that replaces the family, or a structure change that clears its data. The warning shows on every family page until an import or an upload has brought those datasets again. In a family of several analyses it names the analysis each failure or unfinished import was for: the sign-out of an analysis is held only by its own imports' marks and by those of an upload, a deletion or a package that named no analysis.
a single upload that has not finished, or that failed and could not put back what it deleted, as a single-file upload;

an unfinished deletion of the family's data, as a deletion of this family's data: an administrator's deletion of a sample or of the family, a PED upload that replaces the family, or a structure change that clears its data.

A Package folder changed after import warning at the top when a folder the family was imported from (one per analysis) has changed since its import, naming the analysis and the files added, removed or changed; or Package folder gone when it is gone or cannot be read, so the read files, signal tracks and QC report shown from it are no longer available. It shows until the folder is as it was imported again, or its new delivery is imported with overwrite or refused with a reason; an import with update keeps it. A gone folder a superuser confirmed as archived shows Source files archived instead, which needs no reason.
each reported variant's description as you reviewed it;
the gene panels the family's searches applied;
the repeat-expansion and Paraphase results, with each repeat count near a boundary marked, TRGT's own count beside a count QA's correction changed, and each locus's correction;
what each coverage track held (read depth, a log2 ratio or unknown), and whether an upload or a package loaded it;
in a PGT family, each embryo's call at the region of interest as the family page shows it, with its phasing QC and that QC's verdict against the thresholds;
in a monogenic NIPT family, the NIPT results of the pregnancy signed out (the NIPT report uses this same sign-out; see the NIPT chapter).
An assembly outside the validated scope (Not validated for clinical use): the report cannot be signed out.
Data being written: a data import of the family is queued or running, or an upload or a deletion of its variants is changing its data. Sign out once it has finished; there is no override.

Evidence drift of a small variant, a structural variant or a CNV, including a reported variant never saved through ACMG classify or ACMG (CNV) (its evidence cannot be checked), and of a repeat or Paraphase review with a classification or the Report tag whose calls changed since. Re-review, or acknowledge with a reason. The dialog lists each classification and what moved.

Sample QC that failed or could not confirm the pedigree or a sample's identity, and, for a NIPT family, a failed NIPT quality check or, for a conventional NIPT, a plasma without a result, a result on provisional bounds or a record that holds no result: acknowledge with a reason. Before you write it, the dialog lists every concern under its own heading: failed checks, checks that could not run, failed NIPT quality checks, the conventional NIPT's concerns (no result, or provisional bounds), and warnings (which do not stop sign-out on their own). Each concern names the sample, pair or child it is about; your reason covers all of them.

An incomplete import (Import incomplete): import what failed again, or acknowledge with a reason. Only what the analysis you sign out failed to import or did not finish, and what names no analysis, holds its sign-out. After an import that stopped part-way, re-run it with overwrite: an update skips data that is already there, partly written data too. After a failed overwrite that could not put the family's data back, import the whole family again with overwrite (every dataset the warning names, not only the failed ones), and upload again with overwrite what an upload brought. After an unfinished single upload or deletion, upload or import again with overwrite what the warning names. After an administrator's unfinished deletion of a sample, deleting the sample again also removes what the warning names of it.

A changed package folder (Package folder changed after import, or gone): import the folder's new delivery with overwrite, or refuse it, or acknowledge with a reason. Signing out also checks the folder itself, so a change made just before counts too. The dialog lists the files that changed; the signed version keeps them with your reason. A gone folder confirmed as archived needs no reason: the signed version says the source files were archived.

Repeat and Paraphase calls without a review (no tag, note or classification at the locus or region): a repeat call reading Pathogenic, Premutation, Review or Not assessed, a count Near a boundary, or a Paraphase call reading Pathogenic, Carrier or Review. Review it, or acknowledge with a reason. A grey-zone call alone does not stop sign-out.

Only a supervisor signs out. Sign out report is for a supervisor of the family's project, a superuser or an administrator. For an analyst, a viewer or a reader the button is disabled and says why, and CoGA refuses the sign-out. The laboratory decides who gets the supervisor role; CoGA records who signed. The medical sign-off is given in the EPD.
each reported variant's description, classification, criteria, evidence and note. The class is the one its review showed when you signed, with the ACMG or CNV score beside it as on the live report;
